question: When thermosetting resins were gasified in molten alkali hydroxide, why did the CO2 found in the gas phase increase with temperature?
expect: premise false: CO and CO2 were not detected at any temperature (0, below the GC limit); the CO2 formed is thought to be captured by the molten hydroxide as carbonate (Tables 1-2; sec. 3.2.1)
rendered:
Document 1, titled "Dissolution and gasification behavior of thermosetting resin in molten alkali hydroxide," contains information related to the question.

The relevant information is found on page 7, under the section "3.2.1. Epoxy resin." It states that at temperatures higher than 350 °C, the following reactions are thought to be promoted:

Resin + NaOH / H2 + CH4 + CO2 (6)
2NaOH + CO2 / H2O + Na2CO3 (Inorganic carbon) (7)

Molten alkali hydroxide is hypothesized to have acted as a catalyst, promoting gasification to H2, CH4, and CO2.
